subject: tourism
title: Impact of Tourism
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Which of the following is a great challenge for the tourism industry?
questions.answer: D

questions.q: Which of the following is not a positive political effect on tourism?
options: Law and order helps in the flow of tourists
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Which of the following is a positive economic impact of tourism?
questions.answer: C

questions.q: In all-inclusive package tours about two-thirds of the spending goes to:
options: Airlines, hotels and other international companies
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Which of the following is a negative socio-cultural impact of tourism?
options: Cultural exchange between hosts and guests
questions.answer: C

questions.q: The maximum number of people who can visit a destination at the same time without harming it is its:
questions.answer: B

questions.answer: D

questions.answer: B

questions.answer: B

questions.answer: B

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The four main impacts of tourism are economic, socio-cultural, political and ________. (b) The 7-S mantra 'Safai' means ________.
questions.answer: (a) Environmental. (b) Cleanliness.

questions.q: Identify whether True or False. (a) Political impacts are seen more on tourism than tourism impacts on politics. (b) All-inclusive package tours always benefit the local economy most.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: most of the money goes to airlines, hotels and international companies.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) ________ is the foundation of attitude. (b) Societal sustainability can be divided into social and ________.
questions.answer: (a) Belief. (b) Cultural.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Tourism helps keep local arts and crafts alive through the sale of souvenirs. (b) Terrorism increases the chance of developing tourism.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it reduces the chance.

questions.q: Answer in one word. (a) Which organisation defined tourist carrying capacity? (b) Name one country region where general unrest reduced tourism significantly.
questions.answer: (a) UNWTO (United Nations World Tourism Organisation). (b) The Kashmir valley (India).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Foreign tourists bring ________ to a host country, which helps its balance of trade. (b) Construction of roads on mountain slopes leads to soil ________.
questions.answer: (a) Foreign exchange (foreign currency). (b) Erosion.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write any two positive economic impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: Tourism earns foreign exchange for the country and creates jobs for guides, hoteliers, taxi drivers and craftspeople. It also brings tax revenue to the government.

questions.q: State any two negative economic impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: Tourism raises prices and land values at the destination, which hurts local people. Much of the profit leaks to richer countries through imports and foreign-owned hotels.

questions.q: Explain any two positive socio-cultural impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: Cultural exchange between hosts and guests reduces prejudice and brings understanding. Demand for souvenirs and interest in festivals help keep local arts, crafts and traditions alive.

questions.q: Explain any two negative socio-cultural impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: Local youth imitate tourists by smoking, drinking and gambling, and the local culture and identity are lost. Overcrowding and tourists breaking local customs cause friction between hosts and guests.

questions.q: Why do governments of tourist-sending countries issue travel advisories?
questions.answer: Where there is political instability, conflict or terrorism, law and order is weak and tourists are unsafe. The advisory warns their citizens not to go, or to leave at once.

questions.q: What is meant by sustainable tourism?
questions.answer: It is tourism developed and kept in an area so that its resources and features continue for all times to come. It does not degrade or alter the environment.

questions.q: Define tourist carrying capacity.
questions.answer: It is the maximum number of people who can visit a destination at the same time without damaging its physical, economic and socio-cultural environment or reducing the quality of life (UNWTO).

questions.q: Mention any two negative environmental impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: Pollution of water, air and land and the generation of solid waste, and the loss of forest cover and biodiversity because of construction and heavy footfall.

questions.q: Name the 7-S mantras of India's tourism policy.
questions.answer: Swagat (welcome), Soochanaa (information), Suvidha (facilitation), Suraksha (security), Sahyog (cooperation), Sanrachnaa (infrastructure) and Safai (cleanliness).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Mention any three negative environmental impacts of tourism at destination places.
questions.answer: (i) Land use changes, forests are cleared and farmland is replaced by hotels and roads, causing soil erosion and landslides. (ii) Pollution of beaches, lakes, rivers and air, and heavy solid waste and sewage. (iii) Disturbance of wildlife and trampling of vegetation on trekking trails, leading to loss of biodiversity.

or.q: Mention any three positive socio-cultural impacts of tourism at destination places.
or.answer: (i) Cultural exchange between tourists and hosts increases understanding and reduces prejudice. (ii) Community facilities and services improve and are used by local people. (iii) Souvenir sales and festivals keep arts, crafts and traditions alive and give pride in heritage.

questions.q: Explain any three positive economic impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: (i) It earns foreign exchange and helps the balance of trade. (ii) The government earns revenue through taxes, entry fees and import duty. (iii) It creates jobs, including informal ones, and encourages investment in infrastructure.

questions.q: Explain how political stability and instability affect tourism (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Stability and safety attract tourists, and good law and order helps their inflow. (ii) Instability, terrorism or conflict makes tourists avoid the place and their governments issue advisories. (iii) Government policy and political will to build infrastructure decide how tourism grows.

questions.q: Explain any three negative socio-cultural impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: (i) Loss of cultural identity, local language and traditions through imitation of tourists. (ii) Drug abuse, crime and exploitation of children and women increase at some places. (iii) Tourists breaking local norms and the gap between haves and have-nots cause conflict and tension.

questions.q: Describe three ways in which tourism can improve the environment.
questions.answer: (i) Income from tourists funds conservation, cleanliness drives and beautification. (ii) Monuments, parks and gardens are protected and degraded land is put to use. (iii) Local people and tourists become aware of the need to protect the environment and sustainable practices are promoted.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the positive and negative impacts of tourism, giving at least three points for each, in six points.
questions.answer: Positive: (i) Foreign exchange and government revenue. (ii) Jobs, including in the informal sector. (iii) Cultural exchange that reduces prejudice and keeps arts and festivals alive. Negative: (i) Higher prices and leakage of profit to richer countries. (ii) Pollution, waste and damage to forests and wildlife. (iii) Loss of cultural identity, crime and conflict between hosts and tourists.

questions.q: 'The environment is under great strain due to increasing tourism.' Explain the statement in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Forests and farmland are cleared for hotels, roads and garbage disposal. (ii) Roads on slopes cause soil erosion, landslides and floods. (iii) Water, air and land are polluted and resources are depleted. (iv) Flights and local transport release carbon dioxide and other gases. (v) Heavy footfall damages heritage sites, trampling vegetation and disturbing wildlife in sanctuaries. (vi) Waste, sewage and litter are hard to manage and congestion exceeds the carrying capacity.

questions.q: Explain sustainable tourism and the 7-S mantras of India's tourism policy in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Sustainable tourism keeps resources available for all time without degrading the environment. (ii) It balances economic, socio-cultural and environmental factors. (iii) The area's carrying capacity must not be crossed. (iv) The 7-S mantras are Swagat (welcome), Soochanaa (information) and Suvidha (facilitation). (v) Suraksha (security), Sahyog (cooperation) and Sanrachnaa (infrastructure). (vi) Safai (cleanliness) completes the policy, and balance among all these factors sustains tourism.
